quarterly_data.signal: Ciena's 10-K: revenue increased by 19% to $4.8 billion in fiscal 2025 from $4.0 billion in fiscal 2024, with orders significantly exceeding revenue, and backlog (products and services) grew to $5.0 billion from $2.1 billion at the end of fiscal 2024. Ciena believes much of the backlog growth reflects increased demand for connectivity to address AI workloads, with a portion related to an industry-wide constrained supply environment. Remaining performance obligations were $2.1 billion as of November 1, 2025, with approximately 83% expected to be recognized as revenue within the next twelve months.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $5.0 billion (end of fiscal 2025) vs $2.1 billion (end of fiscal 2024); fiscal 2025 revenue $4.8 billion (+19%); RPO $2.1 billion, approximately 83% within twelve months

quarterly_data.signal: Ciena relies on third-party contract manufacturers, including those with facilities in Canada, Mexico, Thailand, Vietnam and the United States, to manufacture, support and ship its products, and says it has experienced supply chain capacity shortages, including longer than normal lead times. As of November 1, 2025 it had $826.2 million in inventory and $2.1 billion in outstanding purchase order commitments to contract manufacturers and component suppliers for inventory (versus $1.7 billion as of November 2, 2024), including advanced orders for certain long lead time components; Ciena may cancel, reschedule or adjust some of these orders, so only a portion is firm, non-cancelable and unconditional.
quarterly_data.figure: purchase order commitments $2.1 billion (November 1, 2025) vs $1.7 billion (November 2, 2024); inventory $826.2 million
